enonce_intro_markdown:
Given that R is 30 km East of P and Q is 40 km South of R.

Calculate:
incertitudes: Q4 : aucune figure imprimée ; le corrigé décrit le schéma (P, puis R à 30 km à l'Est, puis Q à 40 km au Sud de R : angle droit en R). Angle donné à 0,1 degré près (le sujet ne précise pas l'arrondi).

questions.corrige_markdown:
East and South are perpendicular directions, so triangle $PRQ$ has a right angle at $R$, with $PR=30$ km and $RQ=40$ km.

By Pythagoras' theorem: $PQ^2=PR^2+RQ^2=30^2+40^2=900+1600=2500$.

$PQ=\sqrt{2500}=50$.

**Answer: $PQ=50$ km.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) the angle QPR *[4 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the right-angled triangle $PRQ$ (right angle at $R$), the angle $QPR$ has opposite side $RQ=40$ and adjacent side $PR=30$.

$\tan(\angle QPR)=\dfrac{RQ}{PR}=\dfrac{40}{30}=\dfrac43$.

$\angle QPR=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac43\right)\approx53.13^\circ$.

Check with the hypotenuse: $\sin(\angle QPR)=\dfrac{40}{50}=0.8$, and $\sin^{-1}(0.8)\approx53.13^\circ$.

**Answer: $\angle QPR\approx53.1^\circ$ (to 1 decimal place).**
